Persist audit evidence as a content-addressed immutable snapshot and bind its SHA-256 from findings.
Require detailed verification records with tool, version, command, scope, configuration, exit, status, time, evidence digest, revision, and applicable input digests.
Fix repository-root and external-access approval wording and state all six secret scopes as one invariant.
Introduce compatible current schema versions while preserving older artifacts as historical evidence.
projectFacts: Schema 2.1 required verification classes but did not bind artifacts to one audit execution.
No separately owned immutable audit-evidence artifact previously existed.
Remediation plans and executions previously lacked cross-artifact auditRunId enforcement.
End-to-end run-binding fixtures now pass, so audit-code remains lifecycle tested.
assumptions: The user's delegated answers select generated-or-supplied UUIDs, content-addressed immutable evidence, compatible new schema versions, and temporary lifecycle review.
The explicit --proceed token authorizes the four-skill schemas, scripts, tests, documentation, and evidence boundary.
No audit execution, remediation, hosted mutation, secret validation, commit, push, or publication is authorized.
